page.layout: One printed page, one text block in a single column with marginal notes on the right. Running head at top, page number at top right. Below the text, a gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: nũ[?] Plato de Republ. lib.7. & Epinomide; & Aristot.de coelo & mundo, & in libro de mechanicis artibus, quas ita ex Geometria ducit, & praeterea Cicero de natura Deorum 2. & de universitate, & in somnio Scipionis, & in Arato converso: sed in primis principes ipsi Euclides, Ptolemaeus, Higynus, & alii. De his vide & librum sapient.c.7.

XII. LITERÆ deinde illæ, quæ quasvis hujusmodi literas attingunt, & non tàm in generali speculatione versantur, quàm in exemplis, sunt poësis, historia & oratoria facultas: unde major deinde rerum & verborum copia nascitur. Inprimis autem hic Græci & Latini autores cognoscendi.
1. Historia autem res veras sicut gesta sunt aut Historia. sese habent narrat.

2. Poësis res plerunq; fingit, aut fabularum in-Poësis.volucris tegit. Vide Platonem in Ione, & Ciceronem pro Archia, & Plutarchum de legendis poëtis, & de Homeri vita & librorum ejus interpretatione, & Basilium Magnum de legendis poëtis.

3. Oratoria facultas rhetorica, quadam oratio-Oratoria.nis vi & copia, res persequitur. Sed Instrumenta illa, licet nulla sint, sine materia rerum & verborum, quam tractent: tamen commodissimum est illa parata habere: eamq; ob causam primum etiam traduntur, & Plato, ut dixi, παιδείαν[?] vocat.

page.notes: Printed text is in one column; the only marginal notes are "Historia.", "Poësis." and "Oratoria." on the right. The first word of the page is a fragment (the line begins with a damaged abbreviation before "Plato"), transcribed as "nũ[?]". The Greek word "παιδείαν" at the end is set in a worn type and is uncertain. The signature "r 5" at the foot is read from a faint mark. No catchword is visible. Printed spellings such as "tàm", "quàm", "Inprimis" and "plerunq;" are kept as printed.
